value: Land cover legend description for Lebanon. This land cover is selected from the national legend produced by CNRS in 2011 and 2017

An evergreen forest is a type of forest where most of the trees retain their leaves throughout the year, regardless of seasonal changes. The evergreen forest in Lebanon included but not limited to Cupressus spp., Cedrus libani, Juniperus spp., and many others (CNRS, 2011). These forests are characterized by their lush, dense foliage that remains green year-round. The forest can be distinguished by using infrared bands. For the coniferous forests, the vegetation covers more than 70% of conifers and shrubs in the undergrowth (CNRS, 2011).

A cereal refers to any grass plant grown for its edible grains (seeds), which are a staple food source.  Cereals grow in Akkar, North Lebanon, and other areas. The term also applies to the grains themselves, which are rich in carbohydrates. Usually, cereals in Lebanon consists of wheat, barley, and corn
